# `silk/time/zone`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Time zone rules: the [`Zone`](#Zone) type, which tells the UTC offset of a place at each instant and
turns a local date and time into an instant.

## When to use

Use a [`Zone`](#Zone) to show an instant as the local time of a place, or to find the instant that a
local time names. Get a zone by name from the `TimeZones` service of `silk.time.zones`, or
make one from the bytes of a TZif file with [`Zone.fromTzif`](#Zone.impl.fromTzif). [`Zone.utc`](#Zone.impl.utc) and
[`Zone.fixed`](#Zone.impl.fixed) need no data. `silk.time.zoned` joins an instant and a zone into one value.

## Details

A zone holds the content of one TZif file of the IANA time zone database: a sorted table of
the instants at which the offset changed, and the POSIX rule that continues after the last
entry. Because the rule is kept, a zone answers for any year, not only for the years in the
table.

A local time is not always one instant. When clocks go forward, some local times do not
exist. When clocks go back, some local times happen twice. [`Zone.candidates`](#Zone.impl.candidates) returns every
instant, and [`Zone.resolve`](#Zone.impl.resolve) picks one with a [`Disambiguation`](#Disambiguation).

## Errors

- [`ZoneDataError`](#ZoneDataError) from [`Zone.fromTzif`](#Zone.impl.fromTzif) and [`Zone.fromPosixRule`](#Zone.impl.fromPosixRule) if the data is not valid.
- [`LocalTimeError`](#LocalTimeError) from [`Zone.resolve`](#Zone.impl.resolve) if the local time names no instant under the chosen
  `Disambiguation`.

## Gotchas

Leap seconds are not counted, as in Unix time. A TZif file with leap second records (the
`right/` files of some systems) is rejected.

## Examples

### Find the offset and resolve a local time

```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.plain_date_time { PlainDateTime }
import silk.time.zone { Disambiguation, LocalTimeError, Zone, ZoneDataError }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  // Central European time: one hour ahead, two in summer.
  let rome = run Zone.fromPosixRule("CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")
  let winter = Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1795109782)
  if rome.offsetAt(winter).totalSeconds() != 3600 {
    return 1
  }
  // 02:30 on the last Sunday of March does not exist: clocks go from 02:00 to 03:00.
  let skipped = PlainDateTime.fromFields(2027, 3, 28, 2, 30, 0)
  if rome.candidates(skipped).count != 0 {
    return 2
  }
  match rome.resolve(skipped, Disambiguation.Compatible) {
    Result<Instant, LocalTimeError>.Success { value } => {
      // The compatible choice moves the time forward by the hour that was skipped.
      if value.toOffset(rome.offsetAt(value)).time().hour() != 3 {
        return 3
      }
    }
    Result<Instant, LocalTimeError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 4
    }
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 9
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `Zone` with `import silk.time.zone { Zone }`.

## `Disambiguation`

```silk
pub enum Disambiguation
```

How [`Zone.resolve`](#Zone.impl.resolve) picks an instant when a local time does not name exactly one.

<a id="Disambiguation.Compatible"></a>

### `Compatible`

```silk
Compatible
```

For a time that happens twice, the earlier instant. For a time that does not exist, the
time moved forward by the length of the gap. This is the choice of RFC 5545 and of
ECMAScript Temporal.

<a id="Disambiguation.Earlier"></a>

### `Earlier`

```silk
Earlier
```

For a time that happens twice, the earlier instant. For a time that does not exist, the
time moved back by the length of the gap.

<a id="Disambiguation.Later"></a>

### `Later`

```silk
Later
```

For a time that happens twice, the later instant. For a time that does not exist, the time
moved forward by the length of the gap.

<a id="Disambiguation.Reject"></a>

### `Reject`

```silk
Reject
```

Fail with a [`LocalTimeError`](#LocalTimeError) unless the time names exactly one instant.

<a id="Zone"></a>

## `Zone`

```silk
pub struct Zone
```

The rules of one time zone: its UTC offset at every instant.

### Details

A zone owns its table. It is not `Copy`; share it by reference. `ZonedDateTime` of
`silk.time.zoned` borrows a zone. All operations are plain functions, without effects.

<a id="Zone.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Zone`

```silk
impl Zone
```

<a id="Zone.impl.utc"></a>

### Associated function `utc`

```silk
pub fn utc() -> Zone
```

Returns the zone `UTC`, which has the offset zero at every instant. It does not allocate.

<a id="Zone.impl.fixed"></a>

### Associated function `fixed`

```silk
pub fn fixed(offset: UtcOffset) -> Zone
```

Returns a zone that has the offset `offset` at every instant. It does not allocate.

#### Details

The name of the zone is the offset as text, such as `+05:30`.

<a id="Zone.impl.fromTzif"></a>

### Associated function `fromTzif`

```silk
pub effect fn fromTzif(name: string, data: &[u8]) -> Zone
    ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads a zone from the bytes of a TZif file, the format of the files under
`/usr/share/zoneinfo`, and gives it the name `name`.

#### Details

All versions of the format are read (RFC 9636). For version 2 and later, the 64-bit table
and the POSIX rule in the footer are used. A version 1 file has a 32-bit table and no rule,
so after its last transition the offset stays as it is. The zone keeps a copy of the tables;
`data` is not borrowed.

#### Errors

- [`ZoneDataError`](#ZoneDataError) if `data` is not a valid TZif file, or has leap second records.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="Zone.impl.fromPosixRule"></a>

### Associated function `fromPosixRule`

```silk
pub effect fn fromPosixRule(rule: string) -> Zone
    ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes a zone from a POSIX `TZ` rule such as `EST5EDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0` or `<-03>3`. The name
of the zone is the rule.

#### Details

The rule is a name and an offset for standard time, then optionally a name and an offset
for daylight time and the two dates on which daylight time starts and ends. An offset is
hours west of UTC, so `EST5` is five hours behind UTC. A name is three or more letters, or
text in `<` and `>`. A date is `Mm.w.d` (month, week 1 to 5, day 0 to 6 from Sunday), `Jn`
(day 1 to 365, without February 29), or `n` (day 0 to 365), with an optional `/time` from
`-167` to `167` hours. Without a time the change is at 02:00.

#### Errors

- [`ZoneDataError`](#ZoneDataError) with the reason `InvalidRule` if `rule` does not have that form. A rule
  with daylight time and no dates is not accepted.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.


<a id="Zone.impl.isDaylightAt"></a>

### Method `isDaylightAt`

```silk
pub fn isDaylightAt(self: &Self, at: Instant) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if daylight saving time is in effect in the zone at the instant `at`.

#### Gotchas

This is the flag of the time zone database, and its meaning differs by place. In
`Europe/Dublin` the flag is set in winter. To find the offset, use [`Zone.offsetAt`](#Zone.impl.offsetAt).

<a id="Zone.impl.abbreviationAt"></a>

### Method `abbreviationAt`

```silk
pub fn abbreviationAt(self: &Self, at: Instant) -> string
```

Returns the abbreviation of the zone at the instant `at`, such as `CET` or `CEST`.

#### Details

Many zones have no letters and use the offset, such as `-03`. A zone from [`Zone.utc`](#Zone.impl.utc) or
[`Zone.fixed`](#Zone.impl.fixed) returns its name.

#### Gotchas

An abbreviation does not identify a zone: `CST` is used in North America, China, and Cuba.

<a id="Zone.impl.nextTransition"></a>

### Method `nextTransition`

```silk
pub fn nextTransition(self: &Self, at: Instant) -> Option<Instant>
```

Returns the first instant after `at` at which the UTC offset of the zone changes, or `None`
if it never changes again.

#### Details

A change of only the abbreviation or the daylight flag is not counted. The result can be in
any year: after the end of the table, the changes come from the POSIX rule of the zone.

<a id="Zone.impl.previousTransition"></a>

### Method `previousTransition`

```silk
pub fn previousTransition(self: &Self, at: Instant) -> Option<Instant>
```

Returns the last instant before `at` at which the UTC offset of the zone changed, or `None`
if it did not change before.

#### Details

A change of only the abbreviation or the daylight flag is not counted. When `at` is itself
an instant of change, the result is the change before it.

<a id="Zone.impl.candidates"></a>

### Method `candidates`

```silk
pub fn candidates(self: &Self, local: PlainDateTime) -> LocalCandidates
```

Returns the instants at which a clock in the zone shows the date and time `local`.

#### Details

Most times give one instant. A time in a gap, where clocks went forward, gives none: the
result has `skipped` set, with the instant of the change and the offsets on both sides. A
time in an overlap, where clocks went back, gives two.

<a id="Zone.impl.resolve"></a>

### Method `resolve`

```silk
pub fn resolve(self: &Self, local: PlainDateTime, choice: Disambiguation) -> Result<Instant, LocalTimeError>
```

Returns the instant at which a clock in the zone shows the date and time `local`, and uses
`choice` when the time does not name exactly one instant.

#### Errors

- `LocalTimeError.Skipped` or `LocalTimeError.Repeated` if `choice` is
  `Disambiguation.Reject` and the time names no instant or two.
- `LocalTimeError.OutOfRange` if the instant is outside the range of `Instant`.

<a id="Zone.impl.startOfDay"></a>

### Method `startOfDay`

```silk
pub fn startOfDay(self: &Self, date: PlainDate) -> Option<Instant>
```

Returns the first instant of the day `date` in the zone, or `None` if it is outside the
range of `Instant`.

#### Details

This is midnight on most days. On a day when clocks go forward over midnight, the day
starts at the instant of the change, when the clock shows a later time.
